title: Linked lists
summary: A chain of nodes where each one points to the next. Learn to walk, reverse and measure one with pointers.

sections.heading: Nodes pointing to the next
body: Each node holds a value and a link to the next node; the last one links to `null` (`None`). You only keep the first node, the head, and reach the rest by following links.
Adding or removing at the front is instant, but reaching the 100th item means walking past 99 others.

sections.heading: Reversing in place
body: Walk the list once, turning each link around. You need three names: the node before (`prev`), the current node, and the next one, saved before you overwrite the link.

sections.heading: Fast and slow pointers
body: Move one pointer one step at a time and another two steps at a time. When the fast one reaches the end, the slow one is in the middle.
The same trick finds loops: if the list loops back on itself, the fast pointer eventually laps the slow one and they meet.

mistakes: Overwriting `node.next` before saving it, which loses the rest of the list.
